incidents.vector: Compromised business websites display fake Cloudflare verification (ClickFix) overlays that trick users into running a malicious command; the resulting backdoor retrieves its C2 addresses from the Polygon blockchain (EtherHiding).
incidents.impact: At least 31 organizations compromised with persistent backdoors that beacon every minute and survive C2 takedowns, since new server addresses are published to the blockchain for fractions of a cent.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into company servers in August followed by data exfiltration and extortion; a Russia-linked ransomware-as-a-service gang claimed the attack on its leak site.
incidents.impact: Patient, employee, provider and confidential financial data stolen from the operator of 27 hospitals and outpatient facilities in 12 states; extortion threat to publish data and a class action already filed.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to information systems of a subsidiary detected in mid-August; method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Exposure of internal patient ID numbers for 1,400+ U.S. patient records, identifying data for fewer than 50 patients, and contact details for providers and employees; no impact to medical devices or operations, per an SEC 8-K filing.

incidents.vector: Fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA overlays direct users to paste a clipboard-loaded command into PowerShell, triggering DLL sideloading, payloads hidden in PNG images, and a Python reverse-tunnel implant over encrypted WebSockets.
incidents.impact: Attackers gain direct tunneled access into victims' internal networks, used for privilege escalation, disabling security controls, data theft and ransomware deployment, per Microsoft.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion of two Berlin ministries discovered mid-August; attackers exfiltrated data between Aug 7–12 and issued an extortion demand.
incidents.impact: Claimed theft of 5.79 TB of government data including contracts, emails, passwords and classified material, auctioned for 30 bitcoin; Berlin refused to pay. Two ministries cut off from the state network, disrupting housing-benefit and other public services weeks before Sept 20 elections.

incidents.vector: Distributed denial-of-service attack against the Norwegian government network.
incidents.impact: Government network taken offline; a pro-Kremlin hacktivist group claimed responsibility.

incidents.vector: External Microsoft Teams accounts posing as IT help desks placed voice-phishing calls coercing employees to run remote-management tools or custom malware; an advanced variant pivoted to NTLM relay attacks against domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Coordinated campaign (tracked January–April 2026) targeted more than 150 employees across at least 10 companies, attempting persistent footholds and domain-level compromise, per Unit 42.

incidents.vector: Manipulated the thinly traded Tonic token to over 100x its price in 20 minutes, then borrowed assets against the inflated collateral.
incidents.impact: At least $6 million stolen; a further $68 million outflow was blocked when the Cronos blockchain made an emergency halt and rolled back state. Platform reopening in phases.

incidents.vector: Social-engineered access to third-party applications; a four-day intrusion beginning Aug 21 exfiltrated data before discovery on Aug 25.
incidents.impact: Data stolen from oncology, multispecialty and medical-surgical business units of the distributor handling roughly one-third of North American prescriptions; extortionists claim hundreds of millions of records and reportedly demand over $55 million. Customers saw intermittent service degradation.

incidents.vector: Manipulated MAMO token prices to borrow assets with no collateral.
incidents.impact: $8.7 million in crypto-assets stolen; borrowing paused platform-wide. This is Moonwell's fourth hack in twelve months ($6.4 million lost previously).

incidents.victim: Government and diplomatic organizations in Romania, Spain and Türkiye
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures deployed a lightweight batch-script backdoor that abuses legitimate webhook services for command-and-control and exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Initial-access campaigns from September 2025 through April 2026 against defense manufacturing and diplomatic targets, consistent with Russian intelligence collection ahead of Moldova's elections; high-value targets received a faster-beaconing second-stage implant.

incidents.victim: Six cryptocurrency companies on Cosmos blockchain
incidents.vector: Exploited an EVM vulnerability in the Cosmos blockchain platform.
incidents.impact: Nearly $3 million in assets stolen from six crypto companies; Cosmos patched the flaw and froze 99% of the stolen assets pending legal investigation.

incidents.victim: U.S. federal agencies and critical infrastructure (NASA, Federal Reserve, DOE, DOJ, HHS, NIH, U.S. Senate)
incidents.vector: A China-based company operated complementary hacking platforms that mass-infected IoT devices worldwide and routed intrusions through them as an obfuscation network to hide the Chinese origin of attacks, serving customers including China's Ministry of State Security and military.
incidents.impact: DOJ and FBI seized the platforms' hard-coded domains, rendering both inoperable; the operation had targeted U.S. federal agencies and critical infrastructure with activity dating back to 2018.

incidents.victim: Open-source software supply chain (thousands of businesses)
incidents.vector: Self-propagating worm embedded malicious code in hundreds of open-source packages via phished or stolen developer credentials at GitHub and NPM, cyclically compromising developer machines and their tools.
incidents.impact: Australian police arrested two alleged members of the extortion group behind the longest-running supply chain attack spree on record, which harvested cloud keys from 2,500+ organizations via a compromised AI gateway and claimed 3,800 GitHub repositories.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of six SharePoint Server vulnerabilities enabling remote code execution, theft of IIS machine keys, and deserialization attacks for persistence and malware deployment.
incidents.impact: CISA updated its alert (newest CVE added to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog Aug 18) urging organizations to avoid internet exposure, patch, enable AMSI scanning, and hunt for compromise across all supported on-prem SharePoint versions.

incidents.vector: Attack on company servers detected early last week; entry method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Six casinos closed for roughly three days; cash registers, loyalty systems, table games and hotel reception systems disrupted, with some staff temporarily furloughed. Operations resuming on a limited basis while police investigate.

incidents.victim: Government, university, media, technology and gaming web servers (Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada, Vietnam)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Chinese-speaking, SEO fraud and data theft
incidents.vector: Exploited known vulnerabilities in internet-facing IIS and Linux web servers at scale, using AI-assisted exploit generation and a target list of 170,000 URLs, then deployed a cross-platform implant with a Linux rootkit and kernel-level EDR-bypass capability.
incidents.impact: Compromised servers monetized through SEO fraud and data theft, with rogue admin accounts, credential dumping, and persistent backdoors; Cisco Talos assesses the group is operationalizing agentic AI across its intrusion workflow.

incidents.victim: U.S. critical infrastructure PLC operators (water, energy, manufacturing, chemical)
incidents.vector: Internet scanning identifies exposed Siemens S7-series PLCs, then AI-generated exploitation scripts disguised as legitimate monitoring tools gain read/write access to controller memory and ladder logic over the S7comm protocol.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warn of an active threat assessed as persistent reconnaissance and pre-positioning for future disruptive effects; Google separately reports increased targeting of U.S. water utilities' internet-connected PLCs.

incidents.vector: A near-autonomous AI framework of up to eight coordinated agents conducted reconnaissance, credential cracking, vulnerability exploitation and backdoor installation across 12 attack waves over four days in July, requiring no zero-days.
incidents.impact: Personnel records exfiltrated and persistent backdoors installed on government web applications; Taiwan's digital ministry confirmed detecting AI-agent-driven attacks matching the description. Considered the first reported near-autonomous AI attack on a nation-state.

incidents.victim: 322 universities worldwide, companies, and U.S. government agencies
incidents.vector: Spearphishing campaign targeting more than 100,000 professor accounts compromised roughly 8,000 mailboxes across 144 U.S. and 178 foreign universities.
incidents.impact: Superseding indictment charges 17 members of an Iran-based hacking-for-hire institute with stealing 31+ terabytes of research and intellectual property for the IRGC; up to $10 million in rewards offered for five defendants.

incidents.victim: 500+ organizations (healthcare, education, legal, insurance, technology, manufacturing)
incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service affiliates buy initial access, exploit newly announced vulnerabilities within 24 hours (including recent Fortra GoAnywhere and BeyondTrust flaws), and use living-off-the-land techniques for stealth.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA and HHS updated their joint advisory: the double-extortion operation has now hit over 500 victims across critical infrastructure sectors, with healthcare a frequent target; new IOCs published from investigations as recent as April 2026.
